findings_fixed: Test adequacy (lane 2 M1): the reason-normalization guard was only half-pinned — reason='not a plate' + disposition='Moving' is a VALID request body, so replacing the ternary with `$request->input('reason') ?? 'other'` passed all 13 tests while creating a spurious ScanValidation row. Added the driver sibling's test_a_hand_crafted_review_reason_is_ignored_for_a_non_invalid_scan_disposition and PROVED it real by temporarily breaking the ternary.

Cache staleness (lane 3 L1): hits()/recentHits() cache keys were not versioned despite the payload gaining scan_id/disposition, and mapCacheTtl() is up to 15 MINUTES for last_60 — post-deploy the disposition control would silently not render and AC-1 would appear unmet. Bumped both keys to -v2 per the driver's own scanner:map-hits-v2 precedent. NOTE: lane 1 had explicitly cleared this on a wrong short-TTL assumption; the zero-tolerance single-lane-finding floor is what caught it.

Test integrity (lane 3 L3): test_stats_excludes_an_accessible_disposition_hit was a vacuous negative assertion (one hit, assert direct_hits===0) that would go green if the fixture failed to land. Added a positive control asserting direct_hits===1.

Documentation correctness (lanes 1+2): the okf wiki — declared canonical by CLAUDE.md — contradicted the code in three places (missing POST endpoint in scout-api.md's exhaustive table; 'neither surface sets a page tag' in scout-analytics-taxonomy.md; 'no analytics'/GET-only in scout-birds-eye.md). All corrected.
findings_residual: PRE-EXISTING, OUT OF DIFF, FILED AS ITS OWN TASK: BulkDispositionAction and DispositionController pass a null `reason` into Scan::updateDisposition, whose guard `if ($reason !== 'other')` is satisfied by null -> a spurious ScanValidation human-review row per scan (50 selected scans = 50 bogus rows). Same defect class this ticket guarded against. All 3 lanes found it; 2 of 3 classed it non-scoring since this PR neither introduced nor touched it. Durable fix is at the sink (Scan::updateDisposition), which is why it needs its own QA.

PRE-EXISTING (verified unchanged vs base): hits() and stats() cache keys omit the admin's timezone while recentHits() includes it. Two admins in one org with different timezones and the same range share a cache entry and one sees the other's day window. Different defect class from the shape-staleness fixed above.

t4 drops 'Valid'-dispositioned hits from the admin map/Live-Hits (gains Accessible). Driver parity — an explicit approved product decision — but stats() still counts Valid, so an admin can see direct_hits:1 with no marker. This asymmetry already exists on the driver surfaces (accepted in DEV-2059). MUST be confirmed in human QA.

Non-scoring nits posted to the PR as one comment: duplicated reason guard across two controllers; 'disposition-saved' as a bare literal in three controllers with no enum case; mixed auth()->user()/$request->user(); scan_id emitted uncast; org-level admin read cache means admin B sees admin A's dispositioned hit for up to the TTL; buildUrl appends kit_ids[] to the POST; 419 unhandled client-side; the csrf-token meta tag is now load-bearing for the first admin-mode write but unpinned.

ac.evidence: Verified end-to-end over real HTTP as org-2 admin (user 1 via dev-login). GET /scout/org-map/api/map/hits returned scan_id AND disposition on every row — scan_id is the sole gate on MapShell.vue's disposition control, so it now renders. POST /scout/org-map/api/scan/disposition {scan_id:745,disposition:'Accessible'} -> 200; public.scans_metadata.meta->>'disposition'='Accessible'; clarity.hits_hot FINAL scan_id=745 disposition='Accessible' (SyncDispositionToClickhouse mutation landed); platform.activity_log log_name='Disposition' has exactly 1 row, causer_type=user causer_id=1 — attributed to the ADMIN.

Live round trip, and the decisive proof t4 was load-bearing. KEEP: after setting scan 745 to 'Accessible' the hit REMAINED on the next poll (visible scan_ids [708,725,745]) — under the old validDisposition() ({New Hit,Valid}) an Accessible hit would have been DROPPED, so this exact assertion would have failed before t4. HIDE: setting scan 725 to 'Inaccessible' dropped it from the next poll (visible [708,745]) once the CH sync landed. Both admin surfaces carry scan_id, which is what makes the client hiddenScanIds suppression work on the Live Hits card too.

POSITIVE path verified across MULTIPLE kits in the admin's own org — scan 745 (kit 63) and scan 725 (kit 62) both dispositioned successfully, which is exactly the org- vs kit-scoping the ticket required (an admin is no kit's driver). Staging-Live retained: the S-type hit with hotlist_org_id=3 != kit_org_id=2 is returned by both admin surfaces, confirming kit_org_id scoping (DEV-2053) and that actionableDisposition() — not liveActionable() — was used. Driver behavior unchanged by construction (no driver file in the diff). ENV LIMIT: the cross-org NEGATIVE was not exercisable over HTTP because org 2 owns every VISIBLE scan in this seed DB; that case is pinned by test_cannot_disposition_a_scan_belonging_to_a_different_org (404 + asserts no write) and is flagged for human QA.

Derived AC — the defect reusing DispositionController would have introduced. POSTed exactly what map.js sends ({scan_id,disposition} with NO reason key): public.scan_validations for scan 745 stayed 0. activity_log properties show "reason":"other", proving the controller normalized a null reason before Scan::updateDisposition, whose guard `if ($reason !== 'other')` would otherwise have created a human-review row. Also pinned both directions by unit tests, incl. the hostile-key case (reason='not a plate' + disposition='Moving') added in the review-fix round.

Derived AC. A nonexistent scan_id returned a clean 404 (not 500), exercising the same firstOrFail-outside-the-try/catch path the cross-org case uses — confirming the deliberate divergence from DispositionController, whose own test pins a 500 there. The cross-org variant itself is unit-test pinned (see AC-3 env limit).

Not exercisable in this environment: config('database.track_analytics') is FALSE locally, so AnalyticsService::track early-returns and emits nothing regardless of correctness (clarity.analytics count = 0). Pinned by test_disposition_analytics_fires_with_from_scout_and_birds_eye_page, a Mockery expectation asserting BOTH from_scout===true AND page==='clarity-scout-birds-eye' (verified at teardown, so the controller's catch around track() cannot swallow a mismatch). ScoutAnalyticsPage::BirdsEye resolves to 'clarity-scout-birds-eye' as expected. Deferred to human QA / a staging env with analytics enabled.

The approved decision — admins restricted to the 5 driver-facing dispositions — holds server-side: POST with disposition='Valid' returned 422, so the wider admin-only set is rejected even if a client hand-crafts it.
